Fix these first

  1. Unauthenticated Ray dashboard / Jobs API exposed — 10.0.0.5:8265 RG-RAY-001Enable Ray authentication or bind the dashboard to loopback/a private subnet; never expose port 8265 publicly.
  2. TLS certificate fails verification — 10.0.0.5:8888 RG-TLS-001Replace the certificate with one issued by a trusted CA, matching the service hostname and within its validity window.
  3. Unauthenticated Ollama API exposed — 10.0.0.6:11434 RG-OLLAMA-001Restrict the Ollama API (11434) to localhost/trusted networks.

Why this matters

What we observed. Ray’s dashboard API answered an unauthenticated GET to /api/version on the host(s) listed above. Ray has no per-route authentication, so an API that answers us answers anyone who can reach that port.

What that means. The same API serves POST /api/jobs/, which accepts an entrypoint from any caller and runs it on the cluster with the Ray worker’s permissions. That is remote code execution by the software’s own design, which is why CVE-2023-48022 is disputed rather than patched: there is no fixed version to upgrade to, so reachability is the entire control. CVE-2025-62593 is version-specific and is on CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue. This assessment did not determine your Ray version, so treat that one as applicable-if-vulnerable rather than as a confirmed finding about this host.

Why it is not theoretical. The ShadowRay campaign compromised exposed Ray clusters to steal credentials and mine cryptocurrency on rented GPUs, and the clusters were found by internet-wide scanning rather than by targeting.

What we did not do. One benign GET, to a version endpoint. We did not submit a job, did not list your jobs — that response carries each job’s command line, so we do not request it — and executed nothing. No response body was inspected, parsed, logged or stored.

Scope & method

This is an agentless, read-only Level 1 assessment run from outside the hosts. It observes which services are reachable, whether they require authentication, and their transport posture. It does not install software, does not require credentials, and cannot assess cross-tenant fabric isolation or hardware attestation — those need deeper tiers.

Read-only assessment. Detection by observation, not exploitation. No customer payload — no model weights, prompts, training data, inference content, or object contents — was read, stored, or transmitted. Grade thresholds are provisional and will be revised as they are validated.
